title: Deep researcher
description: Answers a question from the corpus this folio ALREADY HOLDS, and stands behind the answer's citations. `agent` rather than `person`, and the reason is the opposite of `librarian`'s: nothing in this loop decides what may be redistributed or what a source means in law — it plans, retrieves, filters and synthesises over material a person has already admitted. The role admits `person` too, and no person-shaped actor is registered for it because none has been named; inventing one would assert a party this repository does not have. WHAT THIS ACTOR MAY NOT DO is report an agent's draft figure description as what the figure shows — `schemas/narrative.ts` holds that line, and it is why an agent performing this is legitimate in the first place. ITS PERMISSION IS IN THE ODRL POLICY, not here: #1186 moved every actor's own `permissions` list into `policies/folio-defaults.jsonld` as an assignee/action rule, and `odrl.test.ts` fails any actor file that still carries one. This actor was written with a `permissions` list about two hours before that landed; the grant itself is unchanged — `content-authoring`, stated once, in the policy.
